title: Overcoming health-related fears – A one-day large-group training session
summary:
The aim of the study is to investigate whether the treatment of a mental health disorder associated with health anxiety is feasible and effective within a one-day training programme delivered in a large-group format. To this end, at least 50 adult participants will be studied. As we are interested in the feasibility of large-group training, a larger sample size would also be desirable. Before our training programme takes place, the number of participants is to be announced via pre-registration.
The clinical sample consists of participants with a mental health condition related to health anxiety. In order to take part in the one-day training session, it is essential to attend a diagnostic appointment in advance, which serves to make a diagnosis and provide information about the exact training programme and alternative treatment options. The diagnostic assessment is to be carried out by trained Master’s students on the Psychology degree programme specialising in Clinical Psychology and Psychotherapy at Ruhr University Bochum. Following the diagnostic session, participants will complete low-stress computer-based tasks (maximum 30 minutes) to measure their levels of certain constructs – such as attentional bias or interpretative bias – which are thought to be associated with health anxiety.
This one-day training course presents effective elements of individual treatment for a mental health condition linked to health anxiety, which have been adapted for use in a large-group setting. The training begins with an information session. Participants are then divided into smaller groups, where various exercises are used to elicit anxiety-related cognitions and situations, thereby enabling them to learn how to manage these feelings and tolerate uncertainty. This includes behavioural experiments, different types of exposure (interoceptive and other exposure exercises in the strict sense), as well as relapse prevention. Furthermore, following the training session, the computer-based task from the diagnostic appointment is to be repeated. As part of a conditioning experiment conducted prior to the training, it will also be investigated whether conditioning or extinction processes of an experimentally acquired fear response predict the success of the training.  In addition, saliva samples will be collected to establish a correlation between the expression and characteristics of certain candidate genes (including NPSR1) and polygenic risk scores, and the outcomes of the training, the results of the computer task and the results of the conditioning experiment.
conditions: The following disorders (according to ICD-10) are included, provided that the individuals experience distressing, life-limiting health anxiety. interventions.name: One-day large-group intervention, at least 50 participants, approx. 9 hours, exposure therapy (interoceptive, and others), behavioural experiment, psychoeducation

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Clinically significant mental disorder associated with health anxiety
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria relating to mental health include the presence of a manic or hypomanic episode; schizophrenia-spectrum disorders; severe existing substance use disorders (except nicotine); and severe post-traumatic stress disorder. On a physical level, exclusion is indicated by an existing pregnancy, severe infectious diseases, acute heart or lung conditions, epilepsy and stroke, intellectual disability, coronary heart disease and a heart attack.
